clue.text: Soak in spice with speed

parts.note: mace is a spice made from the husk of nutmeg
rate means speed, as in 'at a rate of knots'

explanation.surface: A cook marinates something in spice in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To macerate food is to steep it in liquid until it softens.

clue.text: Type of car for peer who lost his main transport?

indicators.note: who lost signals letters are taken away from the peer

parts.note: a marquess is a nobleman ranking above an earl
SS stands for steamship, which carries people across the main, the sea

explanation.surface: A nobleman who has lost his ship looks for a car instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, so main transport is a steamship, SS; 'who lost' removes it from MARQUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A marque is a make or brand, especially of car.

clue.text: Rising curve when tax is added to clothing

indicators.note: is added to puts the tax after the other piece
in a down clue rising means the word for curve reads upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: an arc is a curve
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A rising price curve when sales tax is applied to clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses ARC to CRA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a neckcloth, an item of men's clothing.

clue.text: Dance may be possible when serum banishes painful part

indicators.note: part signals that the answer is a portion of the words serum banishes

explanation.surface: A medicine that banishes pain might let you dance again.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'seRUM BAnishes'. 'painful part' reads as the sore spot; only 'part' marks the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Like an even number, the litany is lacking AI version

indicators.note: version signals the letters are rearranged, after removing the other letters named

explanation.surface: A priest reads a litany missing a section, in a revised version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lacking' and 'version' make a composite: take A and I from THELITANY and rearrange the rest. Al is the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenthly means in tenth place, and ten is even.

clue.text: Bird has no part in capturing first insect

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing

indicators.note: capturing means one piece holds another within it

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word insect

explanation.surface: A bird takes no part in catching the first insect it sees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts I (the first letter of 'insect') inside ROLE, after O for 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriole is a songbird, the golden oriole being the best known in Europe.

clue.text: Note at the end that mistake was found in roan horse from Spain

indicators.note: at the end places the note last
was found in places the mistake inside the roan

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a wrong or mistake
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A vet notes at the end of a report that a fault was found in a Spanish horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is Don Quixote's horse in Cervantes' Spanish novel; 'was found in' and 'at the end' place the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosinante is the old nag ridden by Don Quixote, the most famous horse in Spanish literature.

clue.text: Deliveries to firm at Ulster?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Goods sent to a company in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster looks like the Irish province, but it is a long loose overcoat. An over is a cricket bowler's set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, heavy, belted coat, named after the province where its cloth came from.

clue.text: Appeared to possess tons after estate was first valued

indicators.note: was first puts the estate ahead of the rest

parts.note: E is used for estate, as for an estate car

indicators.note: to possess means the word for appeared holds the tons inside

parts.note: seemed means appeared

explanation.surface: An estate seemed to own tons once it was first valued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to possess' puts T inside SEEMED; 'was first' puts E in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means highly regarded, prized.

clue.text: Getting fresh fire power to back China

parts.note: the rear is the back of something
Ming is a dynasty of China and the name of its prized porcelain

explanation.surface: A country rearms in order to support China militarily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearming is acquiring new weapons, which is fresh firepower.

clue.text: Maintain that a lock will turn

indicators.note: will turn says the word for lock is to be read backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a door lock will turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will turn' reverses TRESS to SSERT. 'lock' looks like a door fitting but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain that something is so is to assert or declare it.

clue.text: One old-fashioned pin up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters of old are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dated pin-up poster of a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one adjective, but 'fashioned' is the anagram signal working on 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a star whose picture fans put on walls, someone idolised.

clue.text: Showing no embarrassment when you were said to pinch a cast off

indicators.note: were said tells us to use how the word sounds when spoken rather than its spelling

parts.note: the word you is spoken here, and it sounds like the letter U
to pinch is to steal or arrest, and so is to nab
to cast off skin or clothes is to shed them

explanation.surface: A shameless thief who pinched a garment and threw it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were said' means the spoken word 'you' gives a single letter by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed means unashamed, not put out or embarrassed at all.

clue.text: New area for product of shellfish

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: A fresh fishing ground is opened for shellfish farming.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining secreted by molluscs such as oysters.

clue.text: Criticise fine song

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil leads
a lay is an old word for a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A critic praises a song as fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay someone verbally is to attack them harshly, just as flaying strips off skin.

clue.text: Doctor relates seizure of gold for top poets

indicators.note: seizure of means the rearranged letters grab the gold and hold it
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a gold theft involving distinguished poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the verb for tampering; 'seizure of' puts the gold symbol inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Poets laureate are appointed national poets, the highest honour in poetry.

clue.text: Family row, long time afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the long time after the row in the sequence

parts.note: a row of things is a line
an age is a long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: A family quarrel that rumbled on for a long time after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is descent from an ancestor, a family line.

clue.text: Was sore after a race had been fixed

indicators.note: after places the soreness behind the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
ached means was sore

explanation.surface: Someone was aching after running a race that had been rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race; 'after' puts the soreness behind the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached means fastened or fixed on.

clue.text: Russian girl can go round in North America

indicators.note: go round means the can surrounds the girl

parts.note: Nadia is a Russian girl's name

explanation.surface: A Russian girl travels around North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go round' puts the girl inside the can. Canada is in North America, so a Canadian is someone found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a person from Canada, a country in North America.

clue.text: Speak ill of Italian leader after the paintings were returned

indicators.note: after puts the Italian leader behind the returned paintings
were returned means the word for paintings is set down backwards

parts.note: art covers paintings as a body of work
Il Duce was the title used by Mussolini

explanation.surface: Someone badmouths Mussolini once the looted paintings had been given back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were returned' turns the paintings word round; Il Duce was Mussolini's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce someone is to slander or malign them.

clue.text: Cut back on leading man's test

indicators.note: back means the word for cut reads in reverse

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of the word man's

explanation.surface: The star of a show has his part trimmed during a trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses AXE to EXA; 'leading' takes M from 'man's'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test of knowledge.

clue.text: Calling me off at the start causes a row

indicators.note: off at the start says the word me is dropped from the front of the calling

parts.note: a calling is a vocation

explanation.surface: A phone call that cuts me off at the outset starts an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off at the start' removes ME from the front of METIER. 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows rising above one another, as in a theatre.

clue.text: Head in charge of a student of current affairs

parts.note: the top is the head of something
L is for learner, a student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A head teacher has charge of a politics student.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to matters of present interest.

clue.text: One who crawls to the bar outside

indicators.note: outside means the bar sits around the other word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone crawls to the pub, stopping outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the bar around 'the'. 'crawls' reads as a pub crawl, but the crawl is a swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bather swims, and the crawl is a swimming stroke.

clue.text: Gives up and loses son to religious thinkers…

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped

parts.note: desists means stops or gives up

explanation.surface: Someone abandons faith after losing a son, like other thinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes one S from DESISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Deists believe in a creator God known through reason rather than revelation.

clue.text: Astonish with a complicated system

parts.note: a maze is an intricate network of paths, a bewildering system

explanation.surface: Someone wows people with an elaborate scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze is to astonish or astound.

clue.text: Father came back with a sheet about how to terminate the attachment

indicators.note: came back means the word for father is turned round

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: about means the sheet goes round the other piece

parts.note: a page is a sheet of a book
to end is how one terminates something

explanation.surface: Dad returns with a page explaining how to close an email attachment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' turns the father word round; 'about' wraps the sheet round the word for terminate.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or attached to a larger thing.

clue.text: or Methodists perhaps for the present

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'or Methodists perhaps for the present' (5): the opening words are missing, so no wordplay for NONCE can be built; a search of the text gave nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: or Methodists perhaps for the present

clue.text: So this can be reassembled by the lifts

indicators.note: reassembled signals that the letters of so this are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic says this machine can be rebuilt by the lift engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be reassembled' rearranges SOTHIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoists are lifting devices, as are lifts.

clue.text: Article that is able to shut out a prickly leaf

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
can means is able

indicators.note: out signals the letters of shut are scrambled

explanation.surface: A botanist describes an item able to keep a spiky leaf away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut out' reads as exclude, but splits into fodder and the anagram signal 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a plant with spiny leaves, imitated in the carving on Corinthian columns.

clue.text: A new filling for food from Scandinavia

indicators.note: filling means these letters go inside the food

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: A new filling for a pastry from Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts A and N inside DISH. The surface hints at a Danish pastry, but here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish describes things from Denmark, a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: Largos? The French adapt them to brisker movements

indicators.note: adapt means to rework, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A composer reworks slow pieces in a French style to make them livelier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapt' rearranges LARGOS plus LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegros are fast, lively musical movements, brisker than slow largos.
